Hi John / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Below is a short recap of what we heard, a conservative TCO sketch based on the numbers you shared, and the next steps we propose. I pulled Rafael and Dylan in to own the pilot and infra plan.

1) Key pain points (as we heard them)
- Gen-only feature set (customer support chat + knowledge base) is driving high per-session cost due to recurring system prompts and long context windows.
- Need strictly bounded latency for live chat (p95 target <= 350ms).
- Procurement/budget window: CFO wants a predictable monthly run rate below $8k for piloted scope.

2) Goals for pilot
- Validate ~10k sessions/mo with p95 <= 350ms and avg cost <= $0.10/session.
- Prove caching and batching levers can reduce compute spend by ~30-50% without degrading UX.
- Provide an audited TCO model finance can review.

3) Token economics (conservative example)
- Baseline assumptions from today’s call: ~1.5k tokens/session (avg), 10k sessions/mo -> 15M tokens/mo generated.
- Redwood hosted model cost (example): $0.0008 per gen token -> $12,000/mo model cost (baseline).
- Infra/serving overhead (instances, networking, etc): estimated $0.003 per 1k tokens -> ~$45/mo (negligible relative to model).

4) Cost-reduction levers we recommended
- Prefix/KV caching: reuse historical context and static system prompts. Expected token reduction: 25-40% for support flows (we model 35% conservatively).
- Batching for high-throughput routes: up to a 20% reduction in compute cost when throughput is sufficient (tradeoff: small p95 increase).
- Model variant + quantization: moving to a quantized variant can reduce per-token compute cost by ~30% at modest quality impact for short responses.

5) Conservative TCO sketch (after levers)
- Baseline model cost: $12,000/mo
- After caching (35% token reduction): effective gen tokens = 9.75M -> model cost ~$7,800/mo
- Add batching + quantization (combined 40% additional compute reduction on top of caching): effective cost approx ~$4,680/mo
- Net: pilot scoped to 10k sessions/mo => estimated run rate ~ $4.5-5k/mo (well under the $8k threshold) - we’ll refine with telemetry.

Attachments: ACME_TCO_Model_v1.xlsx (editable model with inputs) and redwood_pricing_summary.pdf (pricing & pilot options).

Next steps we propose:
- Rafael to kick off a 4-week pilot (instrumented) with sample routes (owner: Rafael)
- Technical kickoff with your infra (Dylan to schedule) - template runbook attached in the Drive link
- Finance review: Marissa + Alicia Park (if you want to include) to sync next week

Please let me know if any of the baseline assumptions above are off (session size, volume, or latency targets). If you’re good, Rafael and I will send a proposed pilot statement of work and schedule a 30-min pricing review.

Thanks -
Marissa

Thanks John - great questions. Quick answers below and a proposed next step.

- Batching vs p95: conservative pilot settings we recommend are max batch size 4-8 depending on route. In our benchmarks for similar support workloads, batching up to 4 increases p95 by ~20-40ms; batch size 8 can add ~50-90ms. With our preferred instance types and routing (we can pin low-latency nodes for chat), we typically stay within a 250-350ms p95 window for short responses. We will instrument p95 in the pilot and enforce SLOs with fallback to a faster model variant if we see regression.

- Caching hit rates & cold-start: for highly templated support flows we see cache hit rates of 30-60%; conservative estimate for your flows is 35% (used in the model). Cold-starts are handled by storing KV cache on persistent volumes for returning users (no cold start for authenticated sessions) and by prefix caching for static system prompts.

- Itemized run-rate: Rafael and I will populate the attached spreadsheet with line items (model runtime, instance charges, data egress if any, and observability retention). That will give Alicia the monthly number as requested.

Proposed immediate next step: Rafael to send a 4-week pilot SOW + schedule a 30-minute pricing/finance review next Tue or Wed (I’m available Wed 10-11am PT). Rafael - any conflicts on your side?

Best,
Marissa
